scales.name: Antagonism
scales.definition: Disposition to pursue one's own interest at others' expense, and to meet friction with force.

facets.name: Callousness
facets.definition: Low weight given to others' costs.

bodyLinks.mechanism: Central serotonin function correlates inversely with aggression, anger and hostility (r ≈ -.12 overall, -.21 in pharmacological challenge studies), and tryptophan depletion raises aggression specifically in people already prone to it.

Congenital adrenal hyperplasia and testosterone therapy shift aggression-related measures, but normal-range testosterone does not — a preregistered trial in 1,000 men found no effect on economic behavior.
bodyLinks.verification: Not applicable to normal variation. Included to state explicitly that the popular 'high testosterone' explanation is unsupported.

items.text: If someone pushes, I push back harder.
items.informantText: If someone pushes, they push back harder.

review.notes: Standing up for oneself is valued in some contexts and censured in others, and the same behavior is sanctioned differently by gender. DIF-test by gender and locale. Per the construct sheet, the provocation framing matters: this is where the serotonin and androgen literatures actually find effects.

items.text: When someone's rude to me, I let it go.
items.informantText: When someone's rude to them, they let it go.

items.text: I'd rather smooth over a conflict than win it.
items.informantText: They'd rather smooth over a conflict than win it.

items.text: I keep an argument going until the other person backs down.
items.informantText: They keep an argument going until the other person backs down.

review.notes: Reworded to remove a negation: agreeing with "I don't ..." makes the disagree side a double negative, which is a known source of respondent error. The pole and keying are unchanged; only the phrasing is now a positive assertion of the same thing.

items.text: I can walk away from a fight I would win.
items.informantText: They can walk away from a fight they would win.

review.notes: High desirability — restraint under provocation is flattering. Retained because it is the cleanest low-pole statement of the facet; matched by r01 and r04.

items.text: I've kept a disagreement going long after it stopped being about the issue.
items.informantText: They've kept a disagreement going long after it stopped being about the issue.

review.notes: Boundary with A2 persistence: rumination after conflict is inward, this is outward continuation. If it loads on A2 it belongs there.

items.text: I've gone out of my way to get back at someone.
items.informantText: They've gone out of their way to get back at someone.

items.text: Even when I've been badly treated, wanting to get even hasn't occurred to me.
items.informantText: Even when they've been badly treated, wanting to get even doesn't seem to occur to them.

review.notes: Extreme low-pole with high desirability — the worst combination in the bank. Lifetime framing makes it harder to endorse casually, which is the only mitigation available without informant data.

items.text: How my decisions land on other people is mostly an afterthought.
items.informantText: How their decisions land on other people is mostly an afterthought.

review.notes: Reworded to remove a negation: agreeing with "I don't ..." makes the disagree side a double negative, which is a known source of respondent error. The pole and keying are unchanged; only the phrasing is now a positive assertion of the same thing.

items.text: Other people's feelings weigh on me when I'm deciding something.
items.informantText: Other people's feelings weigh on them when they're deciding something.

items.text: I've been told I'm blunt to the point of unkindness.
items.informantText: They've been told they're blunt to the point of unkindness.

review.notes: Directness norms vary sharply: the same speech is 'honest' in one culture and 'unkind' in another, and the item is anchored to others' reactions, which are themselves culturally set. Retained because other-observed framing is the only defence against low self-report validity on this scale, but it is the top DIF candidate in the bank and should be the first item cut if locale effects appear.

items.text: Seeing someone upset affects me.
items.informantText: Seeing someone upset affects them.

items.text: If someone's struggling because of a choice they made, that's their problem.
items.informantText: If someone's struggling because of a choice they made, they consider it that person's problem.

review.notes: Political loading: this tracks beliefs about personal responsibility as much as callousness. Watch for correlation with political self-placement if collected; rewrite toward a specific interpersonal instance if it behaves like an attitude item.

items.text: I check whether I've hurt someone without meaning to.
items.informantText: They check whether they've hurt someone without meaning to.

items.text: I can hurt someone and not feel much about it afterwards.
items.informantText: They can hurt someone and not seem to feel much about it afterwards.

review.notes: The highest-stigma item in the bank. Endorsement is rare and honest endorsement rarer still; expect a severe floor effect. Kept because without it the scale has no top end at all — but it must never be surfaced as a standalone statement about the user.

items.text: Causing someone real distress would stay with me for a long time.
items.informantText: Causing someone real distress would stay with them for a long time.

items.text: I assume people are looking out for themselves first.
items.informantText: They assume people are looking out for themselves first.

review.notes: Low generalised trust is rational in some environments and tracks national and neighbourhood context, not only disposition. DIF-test by locale.

items.text: I give people the benefit of the doubt by default.
items.informantText: They give people the benefit of the doubt by default.

items.text: When someone's friendly, I wonder what they're after.
items.informantText: When someone's friendly, they wonder what that person is after.

items.text: Most people are basically straight with me.
items.informantText: They believe most people are basically straight with them.

items.text: I've been proved right about people I was wary of.
items.informantText: They've been proved right about people they were wary of.

review.notes: Justification item: it lets a suspicious respondent endorse the construct without conceding a flaw. This is the only lever available against low self-report validity on this scale when no informant data exists — worth watching whether it out-performs the plainer items. Reworded to remove a negation: agreeing with "I don't ..." makes the disagree side a double negative, which is a known source of respondent error. The pole and keying are unchanged; only the phrasing is now a positive assertion of the same thing.

items.text: I trust people until they give me a reason not to.
items.informantText: They trust people until those people give them a reason not to.

items.text: I assume most people would take advantage of me if it cost them nothing.
items.informantText: They assume most people would take advantage of them if it cost those people nothing.

items.text: It wouldn't occur to me that someone close to me might be using me.
items.informantText: It wouldn't occur to them that someone close might be using them.

citations.title: Revisiting the serotonin-aggression relation in humans: a meta-analysis
citations.claim: Central serotonin function correlates inversely with aggression, anger and hostility (r = -.12; -.21 in pharmacological challenge).

citations.title: Prenatal androgen exposure and sex-typical play behaviour: a meta-analysis of classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia studies
citations.claim: Clinical-magnitude prenatal androgen exposure shifts behavior, including physical aggression and tender-mindedness.

citations.title: Is testosterone linked to human aggression? A meta-analytic examination of baseline, dynamic and manipulated testosterone
citations.claim: Baseline testosterone correlates with aggression at only r ≈ .07, with no evidence of a causal effect from administration.
